definition: Elastic Compute Cloud: virtual servers you rent by the second or hour. Remember: you manage the operating system and patches; AWS manages the physical hardware.
Serverless functions that run code in response to events. You pay only for requests and compute time. Remember: each run can last at most 15 minutes.
Platform as a service: upload your code and Beanstalk handles capacity, load balancing, scaling and health monitoring. Remember: Beanstalk itself is free; you pay for the underlying resources.
Elastic Container Service: AWS's own service to run Docker containers. Run them on EC2 instances you manage, or on Fargate with no servers to manage.
Elastic Kubernetes Service: managed Kubernetes for running containers. Remember: pick it when a scenario mentions Kubernetes or moving existing Kubernetes workloads to AWS.
Serverless compute engine for containers on ECS or EKS. You set CPU and memory; AWS runs the containers with no servers or clusters to manage.
Simple virtual servers, databases and networking at a low, predictable monthly price. Remember: for users with little cloud experience who want a quick website or app.
Adds or removes EC2 instances automatically to match demand, keeps a minimum number running, and replaces unhealthy ones. Remember: this is elasticity, paying only for capacity you need.
Spreads incoming traffic across healthy targets in multiple Availability Zones and runs health checks. Types: Application for HTTP, Network for TCP and UDP, Gateway for security appliances.
Amazon Machine Image: a template of the operating system, software and settings used to launch EC2 instances. An AMI belongs to one Region but can be copied to others.
High-performance disk physically attached to the host server. Data is lost when the instance stops or terminates. Remember: for caches and scratch data, never for data you must keep.
Families tuned to workloads: general purpose, compute optimized for heavy processing, memory optimized for large in-memory datasets, and storage optimized for fast local disk access.
Fully managed batch processing at any scale. Batch queues your jobs and launches the right EC2, Spot or Fargate capacity. Remember: unlike Lambda, jobs have no 15-minute limit.
Racks of AWS-managed hardware installed in your own data center to run AWS services on premises. Remember: you become responsible for the physical security of the rack.
Simple Storage Service: object storage in buckets with virtually unlimited capacity and eleven nines of durability. Remember: new objects are encrypted by default with SSE-S3.
Low-cost archive classes. Instant Retrieval returns data in milliseconds, Flexible Retrieval in minutes to 12 hours, and Deep Archive is cheapest but slowest. Each has a minimum storage duration.
Automatically moves each object between access tiers based on how often it is used. Small monthly monitoring fee, no retrieval fees. Remember: best when access patterns are unknown.
Elastic Block Store: a network drive for EC2 that keeps data after the instance stops. Locked to one Availability Zone and usually attached to one instance at a time.
Elastic File System: managed shared file system that many Linux instances can mount at once, across Availability Zones. Grows and shrinks automatically; you pay for storage used.
Hybrid service that gives on-premises servers access to cloud storage backed by S3, using file, volume or tape gateways. Remember: hybrid cloud storage means Storage Gateway.
Fully managed service to centrally schedule and automate backups of EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and more, including cross-Region and cross-account copies. Remember: one central backup policy.
Point-in-time, incremental backups of an EBS volume. Copy them across Availability Zones or Regions to restore or move volumes. Remember: Recycle Bin can recover snapshots deleted by mistake.
Infrequent Access: lower storage price than S3 Standard, but a per gigabyte retrieval fee. Data is kept across multiple AZs. Remember: good for backups and disaster recovery copies.
Like Standard-IA but kept in one Availability Zone, so it costs 20 percent less, and data is lost if that zone is destroyed. Remember: for re-creatable data.
Cheapest S3 storage class, for data kept for years. Standard retrieval within 12 hours, bulk within 48 hours, minimum storage 180 days. Remember: long-term compliance archives.
Keeps every version of an object in a bucket, protecting against accidental deletes and overwrites and allowing easy rollback. Enabled per bucket; once on, it can only be suspended.
Fully managed third-party file systems. Remember: FSx for Windows File Server for Windows shares, FSx for Lustre for high-performance computing. NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS also exist.
Relational Database Service: managed SQL databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle and SQL Server. AWS handles patching, backups and Multi-AZ failover; you do not manage the server.

AWS's cloud-native relational database, compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL. Storage grows automatically and keeps six copies across three AZs. Remember: faster than standard RDS engines, but costs more.
Fully managed, serverless NoSQL key-value database with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. Remember: Global Tables replicate across Regions; DAX adds an in-memory cache.
Managed in-memory cache using Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached, with sub-millisecond latency. Remember: reduces load on databases for read-heavy workloads.
Data warehouse for analytics and business intelligence on petabytes of data, using columnar storage. Remember: analytics and reporting, known as OLAP, means Redshift, not RDS.
Fully managed graph database for highly connected data such as social networks, recommendation engines and fraud detection.
Database Migration Service: migrates databases to AWS while the source stays fully operational. Handles same-engine and different-engine moves, with schema conversion for different engines.
Fully managed document database compatible with MongoDB. Remember: think of it as the Aurora of MongoDB, with storage that grows automatically across three AZs.
Serverless service to query data in S3 with standard SQL, paying per amount of data scanned. Remember: ad hoc SQL queries on S3 with no servers means Athena.
Elastic MapReduce: managed big data clusters running Hadoop, Spark and similar frameworks on EC2. Remember: when a scenario says Hadoop or Spark, think EMR.
Serverless extract, transform and load service that prepares data for analytics. Its Data Catalog stores table definitions used by Athena, Redshift and EMR. Remember: ETL means Glue.
Virtual Private Cloud: your own logically isolated network in an AWS Region, where you control IP ranges, subnets, route tables and gateways.
A range of IP addresses inside a VPC, tied to one Availability Zone. Public subnets route to an internet gateway; private subnets do not.
Lets resources in a VPC reach the internet and be reached from it. Remember: a subnet is public when its route table points to an internet gateway.
AWS-managed service that lets private subnet instances reach the internet for updates, while blocking connections started from the internet. Classic zonal NAT gateways sit in a public subnet.
Managed DNS service that turns domain names into IP addresses, registers domains, and routes users with policies like latency, weighted, geolocation and failover.
Content delivery network that caches content at edge locations worldwide for lower latency. Remember: also adds security, with built-in Shield Standard and optional WAF.
Dedicated private connection from your data center to AWS that avoids the internet. Consistent performance, but takes weeks or more to set up and is not encrypted by default.
Fully managed service to create, publish and secure REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs at any scale. Remember: the classic serverless pattern is API Gateway in front of Lambda.
Sends users over the AWS global network to your application through two static anycast IP addresses, improving performance and failover. Remember: unlike CloudFront, it does no caching.
Privately connects two VPCs over the AWS network. Not transitive: peering A with B and B with C does not connect A with C. IP ranges must not overlap.
Hub that connects thousands of VPCs and on-premises networks in one hub-and-spoke design. Remember: replaces a complex mesh of VPC peering connections.
Encrypted connection between your on-premises network and a VPC over the public internet. Quick to set up, but performance varies with internet conditions.
Privately connects your VPC to AWS services, other VPCs or partner SaaS services without the internet, NAT or peering. Remember: most secure way to expose a service to many VPCs.
A fixed public IPv4 address that stays yours until you release it and can be moved between instances. Remember: every public IPv4 address is billed hourly since 2024.
Identity and Access Management: a global, free service that controls who can sign in and what they can do, using users, groups, roles and policies.
A JSON document that allows or denies actions on AWS resources, attached to users, groups or roles. Remember: an explicit deny always overrides an allow.
An identity that AWS services, applications or users assume to get temporary credentials. Remember: give an EC2 instance a role instead of storing access keys on it.
Multi-factor authentication: your password plus something you have, like an authenticator app, passkey or hardware security key. Remember: always protect the root user with MFA.
Key Management Service: create and control encryption keys used by most AWS services. AWS manages the hardware, and every key use is logged in CloudTrail.
Records API calls and account activity: who did what, when and from where. Remember: auditing and governance; 90 days of event history are on by default.
Intelligent threat detection that uses machine learning on CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and more. Remember: spots threats like compromised credentials and crypto mining.
Virtual firewall around an EC2 instance with allow rules only. Stateful: return traffic is automatically allowed. Remember: to block a specific IP address, use a network ACL.
Network access control list: a subnet-level firewall with both allow and deny rules. Stateless: return traffic must be allowed explicitly. Rules are evaluated in number order.
Web Application Firewall: filters layer 7 web requests to block SQL injection, cross-site scripting and bad IPs. Deploy it on CloudFront, Application Load Balancer or API Gateway.
DDoS protection. Shield Standard is free and automatic for every customer. Shield Advanced is paid, adding a round-the-clock response team and protection from scaling charges during attacks.
Automated vulnerability management that continuously scans EC2 instances, container images in ECR and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
Records resource configurations and their changes over time, and checks them against compliance rules. Remember: answers what did this resource look like last week, and is it compliant?
Self-service portal for AWS compliance reports like SOC, PCI and ISO, and agreements like the HIPAA BAA. Remember: evidence for your auditors.
AWS handles security of the cloud: hardware, facilities and global network. You handle security in the cloud: your data, IAM, configuration and guest operating system patching.
Grant only the permissions needed for a task, nothing more. Remember: start small and add permissions when required; IAM Access Advisor shows permissions that go unused.
Formerly AWS Single Sign-On: one login to all accounts in your AWS Organization and to business apps. Remember: the recommended way to give workforce users multi-account access.
Uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data, such as personal information, stored in S3.
Dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules in AWS. AWS maintains the hardware, but only you control the keys. Remember: for strict compliance needing customer-managed key hardware.
AWS Certificate Manager: provisions, manages and auto-renews TLS certificates for HTTPS. Public certificates used with load balancers, CloudFront or API Gateway are free.
Stores secrets like database passwords and API keys, with automatic rotation and native RDS integration. Remember: if a question says rotate secrets automatically, choose Secrets Manager.

Central view that collects, correlates and prioritizes security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and partner tools across accounts. Remember: automated best-practice checks now run in Security Hub CSPM.
Guardrails in AWS Organizations that set the maximum permissions for member accounts. Remember: SCPs never grant access, and they do not restrict the management account.
Investigates the root cause of security findings by building visual graphs from logs like CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs. Remember: GuardDuty detects, Detective investigates.
New accounts since July 2025 get a Free plan: up to 200 dollars in credits, lasting up to six months. Always Free offers, like monthly Lambda requests, continue.
Pay by the second or hour with no commitment or upfront payment. Highest hourly price. Remember: best for short, unpredictable workloads that must not be interrupted.
Commit to a specific instance type and Region for 1 or 3 years to save up to 72 percent. Remember: for steady, predictable workloads like a database.
Commit to a steady dollar-per-hour spend for 1 or 3 years to save up to 72 percent. Remember: Compute Savings Plans also cover Fargate and Lambda.
Spare EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off, but AWS can reclaim it with a two-minute warning. Remember: only for fault-tolerant work like batch jobs, never databases.
An entire physical server dedicated to you, with visibility of sockets and cores. Remember: for bring-your-own server-bound software licenses and strict compliance; the most expensive option.
Visualize and analyze your past AWS costs and usage, and forecast future spend. Remember: it also recommends Savings Plans.
Set custom cost, usage or reservation budgets and get alerts when actual or forecasted spend crosses a threshold. Remember: Budgets alerts, Cost Explorer analyzes.
Free tool to estimate the monthly cost of an architecture before you build it. Remember: estimating future costs is Pricing Calculator; analyzing past costs is Cost Explorer.

Checks your account for cost, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operations. Remember: Basic gets core checks only; all checks need Business Support Plus, formerly Business, or higher.
One bill for all accounts in AWS Organizations. Usage is combined for volume pricing discounts, and Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts can be shared.
Technical Account Manager: a designated AWS technical expert who proactively guides your architecture and operations. Remember: a designated TAM comes with Enterprise Support.
Manage many AWS accounts centrally: group them into organizational units, apply service control policies, and get consolidated billing. Remember: multi-account governance.
The most detailed billing data: line items for every charge, delivered to an S3 bucket for analysis with tools like Athena or Redshift.
Uses machine learning on your usage metrics to recommend right-sized EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, EBS volumes, Lambda functions and more. Remember: right-sizing to cut cost.
Digital catalog to find, buy and deploy third-party software, data and services that run on AWS, charged through your AWS bill.
Simple Queue Service: fully managed message queue that decouples application parts; consumers poll for messages. Remember: to decouple or buffer work between components, choose SQS.
Simple Notification Service: publish-subscribe messaging where one message fans out to many subscribers such as email, SMS, Lambda and SQS queues.
Serverless event bus that reacts to events from AWS services, SaaS apps or your own code, and runs scheduled jobs. Remember: formerly CloudWatch Events.
Orchestrates Lambda functions and other AWS services into serverless visual workflows, with retries, branching, parallel steps and human approval steps.
Simple Email Service: send transactional, marketing and bulk email at scale, and receive email. Remember: the answer when an application needs to send email.
Infrastructure as code: describe AWS resources in JSON or YAML templates and CloudFormation creates them in the right order. Remember: repeatable environments across Regions and accounts.
Operations hub for EC2 and on-premises servers. Patch Manager automates patching, and Run Command runs scripts across a whole fleet. Servers need the SSM Agent installed.
Shows the health of AWS services, plus a personalized view of events affecting your resources, like scheduled maintenance. Remember: formerly Personal Health Dashboard.
